narrative:
The model determined that you have a 45% chance of being a bad credit risk. Because this probability is high enough to cross the bank's approval threshold, your loan application was denied.

The three factors that most strongly shaped this outcome were the loan amount you requested, the status of your checking account, and your installment rate as a percentage of income. 

Your checking account status had the largest influence and pushed the prediction toward bad credit risk. Having a negative balance (<0 DM) is relatively uncommon among approved applicants (only 12.6% of them show this status), and the model sees it as a warning sign of financial strain. 

The amount you asked for (2,712 DM) worked in your favor. It is below the average requested by approved applicants (3,020 DM), so this feature helped pull the prediction back toward approval.

Your installment rate of 2% of disposable income also helped your case, as it is lower than the typical 3% seen among those who are approved. This suggests the monthly payments would have been relatively manageable for you.

Unfortunately, the negative signal from your checking account outweighed these positive aspects, tipping the overall decision against approval.

You should focus on clearing or stabilizing your checking account balance, then reapply in a few months with a smaller loan request if possible. This would remove the strongest negative factor the model identified.
